fields.description:
## Context

The noun-based `rebar bridge preview` and `rebar bridge sync` surface now exists. This ticket
makes that vocabulary primary across the CLI, reconciler engine, workflow, scripts, tests, and
documentation. It is an additive expand-contract migration: existing workflows and environments
that still invoke `rebar reconcile`, engine `--mode`, or `--filter-local-ids` must continue to
work with their existing behavior.

The compatibility layer cannot be a naive alias to `bridge sync`. The existing defaults differ:

- `rebar reconcile` with no arguments is dry-run because the CLI wrapper injects
  `--mode dry-run`.
- `python -m rebar_reconciler` with no arguments defaults to live.
- `rebar.reconcile()` defaults to dry-run.
- `rebar bridge sync` with no arguments mutates.

The old entrypoints therefore remain explicit adapters that preserve their own defaults and map
onto the same core planning/execution path. New help, generated references, workflows, scripts,
and runbooks use the bridge vocabulary. The legacy spellings may be hidden from primary help, but
invoking them remains supported. Any future removal requires a separate deprecation decision after
real consumers have migrated; removal is not part of this epic.

## Surface scope and compatibility boundaries

This story makes the CLI and engine bridge vocabulary primary while retaining CLI/engine
compatibility. The public library `rebar.reconcile(mode=...)` and MCP `reconcile(mode=...)`
remain callable at this boundary; sibling `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` adds bridge-shaped library and MCP
operations and must retain the old operations as compatibility entrypoints too.

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mode.py` survives. `MODE_CAPS` and the `Mode` ladder are
still required by:

- legacy `--mode` compatibility;
- the MCP compatibility surface until and after `f789`;
- the phase gate, whose rollback-safe value `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` must remain a real
  `Mode` member so unknown-value handling cannot fail open.

The engine parser accepts both the primary subcommand vocabulary and legacy flags. Both routes
normalize into one internal request before lock acquisition or pass execution; the compatibility
path does not fork state, gate, retry, exit, or mutation policy.

`--filter-local-ids` also remains accepted on the legacy path with its existing write-filter
semantics. In-tree callers migrate to `--only`, which intentionally narrows examination as well
as writes, but the old flag must not silently acquire the stronger `--only` semantics for
external callers.

## Workflow rollback-brake migration

`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` currently runs
`rebar reconcile --mode "$MODE"`. Migrate the workflow and its `workflow_dispatch` input to the
new vocabulary in the same change:

- `reconcile-check` / `dry-run` -> `bridge preview`
- `bootstrap-strict` -> `bridge sync --max-changes 10`
- `bootstrap-throttle` -> `bridge sync --max-changes 100`
- `live` -> `bridge sync`
- stop entirely -> durable `bridge pause` from `1104-93eb-6ce0-4a19`

This keeps the production rollback brake continuously available. The old workflow invocation
remains valid for older checked-out workflow revisions and self-hosted environments.

## Direct callers and references

Migrate both pressure-test scripts from engine `--mode` to primary `preview` / `sync`
subcommands and from `--filter-local-ids` to `--only` where their intent is to bound the entire
validation probe:

- `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_validation_probe.sh`
- `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh`

Migrate the engine tests and external Jira helpers rather than deleting them:

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_filter.py`
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_support.py`
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_user_guide_commands.py`

Primary documentation moves to `bridge preview` / `bridge sync`, while release/migration notes
document the retained compatibility entrypoints and their distinct defaults.

## Test plan

Build a behavioral parity matrix through real CLI and direct engine entrypoints. For every legacy
mode, prove the old invocation and its new primary equivalent produce the same observable plan,
mutation boundary, cap, output class, and exit status. Explicitly prove the two defaults do not
collapse: argument-less `rebar reconcile` stays dry-run, argument-less direct engine invocation
stays live, and argument-less `rebar bridge sync` stays mutating.

Exercise representative phase-gated, paused, in-flight, invalid-argument, and filtered-ID outcomes
through both vocabularies. Prove `--filter-local-ids` retains its legacy write-only filtering
contract while `--only` narrows examination, so compatibility is not implemented by a
behavior-changing flag rename.

Parse and execute the production workflow command-selection block for every dispatch value and
prove the rollback mapping above. Grep shipped workflows, scripts, primary help, and current docs
for stale primary invocations, with explicit exclusions for compatibility registration/tests,
release and migration notes, CHANGELOG, archived docs, and ADR history.

Surface parity census:

- CLI: in scope; new and legacy spellings are exercised through `rebar`.
- Direct engine: in scope; subcommands and legacy flags are exercised through
  `python -m rebar_reconciler`.
- Library: continuity control only; `rebar.reconcile(...)` remains callable and behaviorally
  unchanged. New bridge library operations belong to `f789`.
- MCP: continuity control only; the existing `reconcile` tool remains callable. New bridge MCP
  operations belong to `f789`.
- Automated callers: in scope through the real workflow selection block, pressure-test scripts,
  external Jira helpers, and generated/current documentation.
- Dual direction: in scope; preview remains non-mutating and sync/mapped live modes remain mutating.

No new contention harness is required because both vocabularies normalize before the existing
single pass/lock seams and add no retry, cache, or composed write operation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar bridge preview` and `rebar bridge sync` are the primary documented CLI spellings
      and route through the reconciler engine's primary subcommand vocabulary.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile` remains functional as a compatibility entrypoint. With no arguments it
      remains dry-run; every existing `--mode` value retains its prior observable behavior.
- [ ] Direct `python -m rebar_reconciler --mode ...` and argument-less engine invocations remain
      functional with their prior defaults, while primary `preview` / `sync` subcommands route
      to the same normalized core request.
- [ ] Legacy `--filter-local-ids` remains accepted with its prior write-filter semantics;
      primary `--only` keeps its narrower examination contract. Tests prove they are not silently
      treated as identical.
- [ ] `mode.py`, `MODE_CAPS`, and the `Mode` ladder remain available, and the phase gate can
      round-trip `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` as a real `Mode` member.
- [ ] The library `rebar.reconcile(...)` and MCP `reconcile` tool remain callable and unchanged
      at this ticket boundary.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` and its `workflow_dispatch` inputs use the new
      vocabulary with the exact rollback-brake mapping above; the old command still works when run
      by an older workflow revision.
- [ ] Both pressure-test scripts and external Jira helpers use the new primary vocabulary, while
      behavioral compatibility tests retain coverage of the old engine flags.
- [ ] A real-entrypoint parity matrix proves old and new spellings match for mapped success,
      failure, gate, pause, in-flight, cap, output, and exit behavior without changing the distinct
      no-argument defaults.
- [ ] Every primary help string avoids internal vocabulary (mode, rank, gate, lock, cap, pass,
      binding store, or raw exit-code numbers); compatibility/migration help states the old-to-new
      mapping without changing behavior.
- [ ] Current docs and generated reference use `bridge preview` / `bridge sync`; release notes
      document the mapping, retained compatibility, and distinct legacy defaults.
- [ ] No in-tree workflow or environment breaks merely because it still uses `reconcile`,
      `--mode`, or `--filter-local-ids`.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`: make bridge preview/sync primary; retain the reconcile adapter and
  its dry-run default.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py`: add/normalize primary subcommands; retain
  `--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and the direct-engine live default.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mode.py`: compatibility and phase-gate continuity control;
  must remain.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt`: make bridge vocabulary primary and document migration.
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`: migrate production invocation and rollback input
  without invalidating old workflow revisions.
- `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_validation_probe.sh`: migrate primary invocation.
- `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh`: migrate primary invocation.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py`: primary and compatibility
  entrypoint parity.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_filter.py`: distinct legacy/new filter
  semantics.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_support.py`,
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`,
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`,
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_user_guide_commands.py`: migrate primary test callers while
  retaining compatibility coverage.
- `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`, and
  `docs/release-notes.md`: primary vocabulary plus compatibility/migration contract.
fields.title: Make bridge preview/sync primary while preserving reconcile compatibility
